sections.title: Overview
sections.body:
**Chapter 4:** INFORMATION THEORY FOR MACHINE LEARNING

Author: Your ML Tutor
Date: December 4, 2025
Module: Mathematical Foundations - Information Theory

Topics Covered:
1. Entropy (Shannon Entropy)
2. Cross-Entropy
3. KL Divergence (Kullback-Leibler Divergence)
4. Mutual Information

Why Information Theory in ML?

- Quantifies UNCERTAINTY in data
- Foundation of decision trees (information gain)
- Loss functions (cross-entropy)
- Model comparison (KL divergence)
- Feature selection (mutual information)
- Compression and efficiency

"Information theory is the mathematical theory of communication."
- Claude Shannon, 1948

sections.body:

```python
print("\nExample 1: Coin Flip Entropy")
p_values = np.linspace(0.01, 0.99, 100)
binary_entropy = [-p*np.log2(p) - (1-p)*np.log2(1-p) for p in p_values]

print(f"  Fair coin (p=0.5): H = {entropy([0.5, 0.5]):.3f} bits")
print(f"  Biased coin (p=0.9): H = {entropy([0.9, 0.1]):.3f} bits")
print(f"  Deterministic (p=1.0): H = {entropy([1.0]):.3f} bits")
```

sections.title: Example 3: Weather prediction
sections.body:
**What this code covers**

- SECTION 2: CROSS-ENTROPY - COMPARING DISTRIBUTIONS…
- Calculate cross-entropy H(P,Q)
- Plot 1: Binary entropy function
- Plot 2: Entropy comparison
- Plot 3: Distribution visualization
- Plot 4: Entropy vs number of outcomes (uniform)

```python
print("\nExample 3: Weather Entropy")
weather_uniform = [0.25, 0.25, 0.25, 0.25]  # Sunny, Rainy, Cloudy, Snowy
weather_predictable = [0.7, 0.2, 0.08, 0.02]  # Usually sunny

print(f"  Unpredictable weather: H = {entropy(weather_uniform):.3f} bits")
print(f"  Predictable weather: H = {entropy(weather_predictable):.3f} bits")

# Visualizations
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(14, 10))

# Plot 1: Binary entropy function
axes[0, 0].plot(p_values, binary_entropy, linewidth=3, color='blue')
axes[0, 0].axvline(0.5, color='red', linestyle='--', linewidth=2, 
                   label='Maximum at p=0.5')
axes[0, 0].scatter([0.5], [1.0], s=200, c='red', zorder=5)
axes[0, 0].set_xlabel('p (probability of heads)', fontsize=12)
axes[0, 0].set_ylabel('H(p) in bits', fontsize=12)
axes[0, 0].set_title('Binary Entropy Function', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
axes[0, 0].legend(fontsize=11)
axes[0, 0].grid(True, alpha=0.3)
axes[0, 0].set_ylim(0, 1.1)

# Add annotations
axes[0, 0].annotate('Maximum uncertainty\n(fair coin)', 
                    xy=(0.5, 1.0), xytext=(0.3, 0.85),
                    arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', lw=2),
                    fontsize=10, bbox=dict(boxstyle='round', facecolor='yellow'))
axes[0, 0].annotate('Low uncertainty\n(biased coin)', 
                    xy=(0.9, entropy([0.9, 0.1])), xytext=(0.7, 0.3),
                    arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', lw=2),
                    fontsize=10, bbox=dict(boxstyle='round', facecolor='lightblue'))

# Plot 2: Entropy comparison
distributions = ['Fair\nCoin', 'Biased\nCoin\n(0.9)', 'Fair\nDie', 'Loaded\nDie', 
                'Uniform\nWeather', 'Predictable\nWeather']
entropies = [
    entropy([0.5, 0.5]),
    entropy([0.9, 0.1]),
    entropy(fair_die),
    entropy(loaded_die),
    entropy(weather_uniform),
    entropy(weather_predictable)
]
colors = ['green', 'lightgreen', 'blue', 'lightblue', 'purple', 'pink']

bars = axes[0, 1].bar(range(len(distributions)), entropies, color=colors, 
                       alpha=0.7, edgecolor='black', linewidth=2)
axes[0, 1].set_ylabel('Entropy (bits)', fontsize=12)
axes[0, 1].set_title('Entropy Comparison', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
axes[0, 1].set_xticks(range(len(distributions)))
axes[0, 1].set_xticklabels(distributions, fontsize=9)
axes[0, 1].grid(True, alpha=0.3, axis='y')

for bar, ent in zip(bars, entropies):
    height = bar.get_height()
    axes[0, 1].text(bar.get_x() + bar.get_width()/2, height + 0.05, 
                    f'{ent:.2f}', ha='center', fontsize=10, fontweight='bold')

# Plot 3: Distribution visualization
x = np.arange(6)
width = 0.35

axes[1, 0].bar(x - width/2, fair_die, width, label='Fair Die', 
               color='blue', alpha=0.7, edgecolor='black')
axes[1, 0].bar(x + width/2, loaded_die, width, label='Loaded Die', 
               color='red', alpha=0.7, edgecolor='black')
axes[1, 0].set_xlabel('Outcome', fontsize=12)
axes[1, 0].set_ylabel('Probability', fontsize=12)
axes[1, 0].set_title('Fair vs Loaded Die Distributions', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
axes[1, 0].set_xticks(x)
axes[1, 0].set_xticklabels(['1', '2', '3', '4', '5', '6'])
axes[1, 0].legend(fontsize=11)
axes[1, 0].grid(True, alpha=0.3, axis='y')

# Plot 4: Entropy vs number of outcomes (uniform)
n_outcomes = np.arange(2, 21)
max_entropy = np.log2(n_outcomes)

axes[1, 1].plot(n_outcomes, max_entropy, 'o-', linewidth=2, markersize=8, color='purple')
axes[1, 1].set_xlabel('Number of Equally Likely Outcomes', fontsize=12)
axes[1, 1].set_ylabel('Maximum Entropy (bits)', fontsize=12)
axes[1, 1].set_title('Entropy Grows with Uncertainty', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
axes[1, 1].grid(True, alpha=0.3)

# Add examples
axes[1, 1].scatter([2], [1], s=200, c='red', zorder=5)
axes[1, 1].text(2, 1.2, 'Coin', fontsize=10, ha='center', fontweight='bold')
axes[1, 1].scatter([6], [np.log2(6)], s=200, c='blue', zorder=5)
axes[1, 1].text(6, np.log2(6)+0.2, 'Die', fontsize=10, ha='center', fontweight='bold')

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('entropy_basics.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
print("\n✓ Saved entropy visualization")

"""
================================================================================
SECTION 2: CROSS-ENTROPY - COMPARING DISTRIBUTIONS
================================================================================

VISUAL INTUITION:
-----------------
True distribution P:     Model prediction Q:
    🍎 🍊                   🍎 🍊
    60% 40%                 50% 50%

Cross-Entropy H(P,Q) = How much information needed if we use 
                        wrong distribution Q to encode data from P

Perfect match (P=Q) → H(P,Q) = H(P)
Mismatch → H(P,Q) > H(P) (penalty for being wrong!)

SIMPLE EXPLANATION:
-------------------
Cross-Entropy measures:
"How surprised am I if I believe Q, but truth is P?"

• In ML: Loss function for classification!
• Penalizes confident wrong predictions more
• Equivalent to negative log-likelihood
• Minimizing cross-entropy = maximizing likelihood

REAL-WORLD USE CASES:
---------------------
• Neural Networks: Cross-entropy loss for classification
• Language Models: Perplexity = exp(cross-entropy)
• Model Training: Gradient descent minimizes H(P,Q)
• Compression: Optimal code length

KEY CONCEPTS:
-------------
1. Cross-Entropy:
   H(P,Q) = -Σ p(x) log₂(q(x))
   
   Where:
   - P = true distribution
   - Q = predicted/model distribution
   
2. Binary Cross-Entropy:
   H(P,Q) = -[p log(q) + (1-p) log(1-q)]
   
3. Properties:
   - H(P,Q) ≥ H(P) (equality when P=Q)
   - Not symmetric: H(P,Q) ≠ H(Q,P)
   - Used as loss function in ML

4. Relationship to MLE:
   Minimizing cross-entropy = Maximizing log-likelihood!

MATH:
-----
Example: True=[0.6, 0.4], Predicted=[0.5, 0.5]
H(P,Q) = -0.6 log₂(0.5) - 0.4 log₂(0.5)
       = -0.6(-1) - 0.4(-1)
       = 1.0 bit

If perfect: True=[0.6, 0.4], Predicted=[0.6, 0.4]
H(P,P) = -0.6 log₂(0.6) - 0.4 log₂(0.4)
       ≈ 0.971 bits (better!)
"""

print("\n" + "="*80)
print("SECTION 2: CROSS-ENTROPY")
print("="*80)

def cross_entropy(p, q):
    """Calculate cross-entropy H(P,Q)"""
    p = np.array(p)
    q = np.array(q)
    # Avoid log(0)
    q = np.clip(q, 1e-10, 1.0)
    return -np.sum(p * np.log2(q))
```

sections.title: Example 1: Binary classification
sections.body:
```python
print("\nExample 1: Binary Classification")
true_label = [1, 0]  # Class 1

# Different model predictions
confident_correct = [0.9, 0.1]
uncertain = [0.6, 0.4]
confident_wrong = [0.1, 0.9]

ce_correct = cross_entropy(true_label, confident_correct)
ce_uncertain = cross_entropy(true_label, uncertain)
ce_wrong = cross_entropy(true_label, confident_wrong)

print(f"  True: {true_label}")
print(f"  Confident & correct [0.9, 0.1]: CE = {ce_correct:.3f} bits")
print(f"  Uncertain [0.6, 0.4]: CE = {ce_uncertain:.3f} bits")
print(f"  Confident & wrong [0.1, 0.9]: CE = {ce_wrong:.3f} bits")
print(f"\n  🎯 Confident wrong predictions get high penalty!")
```

sections.title: Example 3: Language modeling
sections.body:
**What this code covers**

- SECTION 3: KL DIVERGENCE - DISTANCE BETWEEN DISTRIBUTIONS…
- Calculate KL divergence KL(P||Q)
- Plot 1: Binary cross-entropy surface
- Plot 2: Comparison for different predictions
- Plot 3: True vs predicted distributions
- Plot 4: Training progress (CE decreasing)
- Simulate decreasing cross-entropy during training
- Avoid division by zero

```python
print("\nExample 3: Language Model (Next word prediction)")
true_word = [0, 1, 0, 0, 0]  # Word index 1
vocab_size = 5

uniform_pred = [0.2] * 5  # Random guessing
informed_pred = [0.1, 0.6, 0.15, 0.1, 0.05]  # Learned model

ce_uniform = cross_entropy(true_word, uniform_pred)
ce_informed = cross_entropy(true_word, informed_pred)

print(f"  Random guess: CE = {ce_uniform:.3f} bits")
print(f"  Trained model: CE = {ce_informed:.3f} bits")
print(f"  Improvement: {ce_uniform - ce_informed:.3f} bits")

# Visualizations
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(14, 10))

# Plot 1: Binary cross-entropy surface
p_true = 0.7  # True probability
q_range = np.linspace(0.01, 0.99, 100)
ce_values = [-p_true * np.log2(q) - (1-p_true) * np.log2(1-q) for q in q_range]

axes[0, 0].plot(q_range, ce_values, linewidth=3, color='red')
axes[0, 0].axvline(p_true, color='green', linestyle='--', linewidth=2, 
                   label=f'True p={p_true}')
axes[0, 0].scatter([p_true], [-p_true * np.log2(p_true) - (1-p_true) * np.log2(1-p_true)], 
                   s=200, c='green', zorder=5)
axes[0, 0].set_xlabel('Predicted Probability q', fontsize=12)
axes[0, 0].set_ylabel('Cross-Entropy Loss', fontsize=12)
axes[0, 0].set_title(f'Binary Cross-Entropy (True p={p_true})', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
axes[0, 0].legend(fontsize=11)
axes[0, 0].grid(True, alpha=0.3)
axes[0, 0].set_ylim(0, 6)

# Plot 2: Comparison for different predictions
predictions_names = ['Confident\nCorrect', 'Uncertain', 'Confident\nWrong']
ce_values_comp = [ce_correct, ce_uncertain, ce_wrong]
colors_comp = ['green', 'yellow', 'red']

bars = axes[0, 1].bar(predictions_names, ce_values_comp, color=colors_comp, 
                       alpha=0.7, edgecolor='black', linewidth=2)
axes[0, 1].set_ylabel('Cross-Entropy Loss', fontsize=12)
axes[0, 1].set_title('Penalty for Wrong Predictions', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
axes[0, 1].grid(True, alpha=0.3, axis='y')

for bar, ce in zip(bars, ce_values_comp):
    height = bar.get_height()
    axes[0, 1].text(bar.get_x() + bar.get_width()/2, height + 0.1, 
                    f'{ce:.2f}', ha='center', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')

# Plot 3: True vs predicted distributions
classes = ['Class 0', 'Class 1', 'Class 2']
x_pos = np.arange(len(classes))
width = 0.25

axes[1, 0].bar(x_pos - width, true_dist, width, label='True', 
               color='blue', alpha=0.7, edgecolor='black')
axes[1, 0].bar(x_pos, pred1, width, label='Good (CE=0.32)', 
               color='green', alpha=0.7, edgecolor='black')
axes[1, 0].bar(x_pos + width, pred3, width, label='Bad (CE=2.32)', 
               color='red', alpha=0.7, edgecolor='black')
axes[1, 0].set_ylabel('Probability', fontsize=12)
axes[1, 0].set_title('Multi-class Predictions', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
axes[1, 0].set_xticks(x_pos)
axes[1, 0].set_xticklabels(classes)
axes[1, 0].legend(fontsize=10)
axes[1, 0].grid(True, alpha=0.3, axis='y')

# Plot 4: Training progress (CE decreasing)
epochs = np.arange(0, 100)
# Simulate decreasing cross-entropy during training
initial_ce = 2.5
final_ce = 0.3
ce_over_time = initial_ce * np.exp(-0.05 * epochs) + final_ce

axes[1, 1].plot(epochs, ce_over_time, linewidth=3, color='blue')
axes[1, 1].fill_between(epochs, ce_over_time, final_ce, alpha=0.3, color='blue')
axes[1, 1].axhline(final_ce, color='green', linestyle='--', linewidth=2, 
                   label='Converged value')
axes[1, 1].set_xlabel('Training Epoch', fontsize=12)
axes[1, 1].set_ylabel('Cross-Entropy Loss', fontsize=12)
axes[1, 1].set_title('Training: Minimizing Cross-Entropy', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
axes[1, 1].legend(fontsize=11)
axes[1, 1].grid(True, alpha=0.3)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('cross_entropy.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
print("\n✓ Saved cross-entropy visualization")

"""
================================================================================
SECTION 3: KL DIVERGENCE - DISTANCE BETWEEN DISTRIBUTIONS
================================================================================

VISUAL INTUITION:
-----------------
True distribution P:    Model Q:
    📊                  📊
   ╱ ╲                ╱  ╲
  ╱   ╲              ╱    ╲
 ╱     ╲            ╱      ╲

KL(P||Q) = "How different is Q from P?"

• KL = 0 → Distributions identical
• KL > 0 → Distributions different
• Large KL → Very different!

SIMPLE EXPLANATION:
-------------------
KL Divergence (Kullback-Leibler):
"Extra bits needed to encode P using code optimized for Q"

• NOT a true distance (not symmetric!)
• KL(P||Q) ≠ KL(Q||P)
• Always ≥ 0
• Used to compare model to truth

REAL-WORLD USE CASES:
---------------------
• Variational Autoencoders (VAE): KL regularization
• Reinforcement Learning: Policy optimization
• Model Comparison: Which model fits data better?
• Generative Models: Matching distributions

KEY CONCEPTS:
-------------
1. KL Divergence:
   KL(P||Q) = Σ p(x) log₂(p(x)/q(x))
            = H(P,Q) - H(P)
            = Cross-entropy - Entropy
   
2. Properties:
   - KL(P||Q) ≥ 0 (Gibbs' inequality)
   - KL(P||Q) = 0 iff P = Q
   - NOT symmetric: KL(P||Q) ≠ KL(Q||P)
   
3. Interpretation:
   "Information gained when revising belief from Q to P"
   "Relative entropy of P with respect to Q"

4. Relationship:
   KL(P||Q) = H(P,Q) - H(P)
   
   If P fixed, minimizing KL = minimizing cross-entropy!

MATH:
-----
Example: P=[0.5, 0.5], Q=[0.7, 0.3]

KL(P||Q) = 0.5 log₂(0.5/0.7) + 0.5 log₂(0.5/0.3)
         = 0.5(-0.485) + 0.5(0.737)
         ≈ 0.126 bits

KL(Q||P) = 0.7 log₂(0.7/0.5) + 0.3 log₂(0.3/0.5)
         = 0.7(0.485) + 0.3(-0.737)
         ≈ 0.118 bits

Note: KL(P||Q) ≠ KL(Q||P)!
"""

print("\n" + "="*80)
print("SECTION 3: KL DIVERGENCE")
print("="*80)

def kl_divergence(p, q):
    """Calculate KL divergence KL(P||Q)"""
    p = np.array(p)
    q = np.array(q)
    # Avoid division by zero
    q = np.clip(q, 1e-10, 1.0)
    p = np.clip(p, 1e-10, 1.0)
    return np.sum(p * np.log2(p / q))
```

![Cross Entropy](/ml-img/cross-entropy-45d5ed1f.png)

sections.title: Example 1: Symmetric vs Asymmetric
sections.body:
```python
print("\nExample 1: Asymmetry of KL Divergence")
p = [0.5, 0.5]
q = [0.7, 0.3]

kl_pq = kl_divergence(p, q)
kl_qp = kl_divergence(q, p)

print(f"  P = {p}")
print(f"  Q = {q}")
print(f"  KL(P||Q) = {kl_pq:.4f} bits")
print(f"  KL(Q||P) = {kl_qp:.4f} bits")
print(f"  Different? {kl_pq != kl_qp} ✓")
```

sections.title: Example 2: Model comparison
sections.body:
```python
print("\nExample 2: Comparing Two Models to True Distribution")
true_dist = [0.3, 0.5, 0.2]

model1 = [0.35, 0.45, 0.2]  # Close to truth
model2 = [0.1, 0.1, 0.8]    # Far from truth

kl1 = kl_divergence(true_dist, model1)
kl2 = kl_divergence(true_dist, model2)

print(f"  True distribution: {true_dist}")
print(f"  Model 1: {model1}, KL = {kl1:.4f} bits")
print(f"  Model 2: {model2}, KL = {kl2:.4f} bits")
print(f"  Model 1 is better! (lower KL)")
```

sections.title: Example 3: Vae regularization
sections.body:
**What this code covers**

- Plot 1: KL divergence surface (2D case)
- Plot 2: Comparison with entropy and cross-entropy
- Plot 3: Model comparison bars
- Plot 4: KL in optimization
- Simulate KL divergence decreasing during training

```python
print("\nExample 3: VAE - Matching to Prior")
prior = [0.25, 0.25, 0.25, 0.25]  # Uniform prior
learned_dist1 = [0.27, 0.24, 0.25, 0.24]  # Close to prior
learned_dist2 = [0.7, 0.1, 0.1, 0.1]  # Far from prior

kl_prior1 = kl_divergence(learned_dist1, prior)
kl_prior2 = kl_divergence(learned_dist2, prior)

print(f"  Prior (uniform): {prior}")
print(f"  Latent dist 1: {learned_dist1}, KL = {kl_prior1:.4f}")
print(f"  Latent dist 2: {learned_dist2}, KL = {kl_prior2:.4f}")
print(f"  Lower KL → Better matches prior (VAE regularization)")

# Visualizations
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(14, 10))

# Plot 1: KL divergence surface (2D case)
p_fixed = 0.7
q_range = np.linspace(0.01, 0.99, 100)
kl_pq_range = [kl_divergence([p_fixed, 1-p_fixed], [q, 1-q]) for q in q_range]
kl_qp_range = [kl_divergence([q, 1-q], [p_fixed, 1-p_fixed]) for q in q_range]

axes[0, 0].plot(q_range, kl_pq_range, linewidth=2.5, color='blue', label='KL(P||Q)')
axes[0, 0].plot(q_range, kl_qp_range, linewidth=2.5, color='red', linestyle='--', label='KL(Q||P)')
axes[0, 0].axvline(p_fixed, color='green', linestyle=':', linewidth=2, label=f'P (p={p_fixed})')
axes[0, 0].scatter([p_fixed], [0], s=200, c='green', zorder=5, marker='*')
axes[0, 0].set_xlabel('Q (predicted probability)', fontsize=12)
axes[0, 0].set_ylabel('KL Divergence (bits)', fontsize=12)
axes[0, 0].set_title(f'KL Divergence (P fixed at p={p_fixed})', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
axes[0, 0].legend(fontsize=11)
axes[0, 0].grid(True, alpha=0.3)
axes[0, 0].set_ylim(0, 3)

# Plot 2: Comparison with entropy and cross-entropy
categories_info = ['H(P)\nEntropy', 'H(P,Q)\nCross-Ent', 'KL(P||Q)\nDivergence']
p_ex = [0.6, 0.4]
q_ex = [0.5, 0.5]

h_p = entropy(p_ex)
h_pq = cross_entropy(p_ex, q_ex)
kl_ex = kl_divergence(p_ex, q_ex)

values_info = [h_p, h_pq, kl_ex]
colors_info = ['blue', 'orange', 'red']

bars = axes[0, 1].bar(categories_info, values_info, color=colors_info, 
                       alpha=0.7, edgecolor='black', linewidth=2)
axes[0, 1].set_ylabel('Bits', fontsize=12)
axes[0, 1].set_title('Relationship: H(P,Q) = H(P) + KL(P||Q)', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
axes[0, 1].grid(True, alpha=0.3, axis='y')

for bar, val in zip(bars, values_info):
    height = bar.get_height()
    axes[0, 1].text(bar.get_x() + bar.get_width()/2, height + 0.02, 
                    f'{val:.3f}', ha='center', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')

# Add equation
axes[0, 1].text(0.5, 0.85, f'{h_pq:.3f} = {h_p:.3f} + {kl_ex:.3f}', 
                transform=axes[0, 1].transAxes, fontsize=12, ha='center',
                bbox=dict(boxstyle='round', facecolor='yellow'))

# Plot 3: Model comparison bars
models = ['True\nDistribution', 'Model 1\n(Close)', 'Model 2\n(Far)']
x_comp = np.arange(3)
distribs = [true_dist, model1, model2]
colors_models = ['blue', 'green', 'red']

for i, (dist, color) in enumerate(zip(distribs, colors_models)):
    axes[1, 0].bar(x_comp + i*0.25, dist, 0.25, label=models[i], 
                   color=color, alpha=0.7, edgecolor='black')

axes[1, 0].set_xlabel('Class', fontsize=12)
axes[1, 0].set_ylabel('Probability', fontsize=12)
axes[1, 0].set_title(f'Model Comparison (KL₁={kl1:.3f}, KL₂={kl2:.3f})', 
                     fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')

axes[1, 0].legend(fontsize=10)

# Plot 4: KL in optimization
# Simulate KL divergence decreasing during training

axes[1, 1].semilogy(epochs_kl, kl_over_time, linewidth=3, color='purple')
```
